title: Inference request topology & console debugging lab - Everbrook
transcript_header: Date: 2026-10-14 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Recording: Fireflies.ai | Meeting ID: fireflies-8f3b2a9e | Location: video call
summary: Console deep-dive: Redwood SE walked Everbrook through the request topology and debugging flows in the Console. Focus on request trace stitching, per-token latency hotspots, KV-cache behaviors, and routing fallbacks. Customer raised SSO/KMS/residency questions and latency vs cost tradeoffs for Dedicated vs Hosted. Agreed to a 3-week POC pilot to run benchmark traces and a canary rollout plan.
topics: KV cache / prefix cache behavior and mis-hits
model routing, fallback policies, dedicated vs hosted
security: SAML SSO, KMS, audit logs, SOC 2
action_items: Priya Patel | Share Everbrook sample request traces (anonymized) and typical sequence length distribution | Due: 2026-10-18
Diego Alvarez | Export console trace map for example trace and annotate hotspot points, send notes | Due: 2026-10-16
Maya Chen | Send POC statement of work + pricing options (hosted vs dedicated) and SSO/KMS checklist | Due: 2026-10-15
next_steps: Redwood -> send POC SOW and security pack
Everbrook -> provide 48 sample request traces + peak qps estimates
Schedule 1hr POC kickoff the week of 2026-10-20
SE-run micro-benchmark on customer sample workload (token-level latency)
transcript: [00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 40 minutes, Diego will take you through the Console debugging lab and then we'll do Q&A. Quick intros?
[00:12] Priya (Everbrook): Hi I'm Priya, lead on ML infra, we run the customer chat assistant and some risk models. Mostly concerned about tail latency and PII redaction flows.
[00:25] Owen (Everbrook SRE): Owen, infra, we'll own deployment and networking, VPCs, peering, that sort of thing.
[00:33] Lena (Security): Lena here, security/compliance. SOC2, KMS, audit logs are key for us.
[00:40] Samir (Product): Samir, product, interested in rollout tooling and A/B canaries.

[00:47] Diego (Redwood SE): Awesome. I'll share my screen — hitting the request topology map in Console. Note: sometimes the product name shows as "Redwood Decide" in the ASR, sorry, it's Redwood Dedicated/Hosted variants.

[01:05] Diego: Starting with a synthetic trace — top shows the request flow: API ingress, routing layer, model runner, KV cache lookup, and postprocessing. The flamegraph on the right is per-token latency. You can see a few red hotspots around the 3rd-6th token in this example.
[01:28] Priya: That spike — is that decoding or KV cache miss? In our infra we see intermittent blips when we do long-prefix prompts.

[01:37] Diego: Good question. In this trace it's a KV miss cascading into a full KV recompute and the kernel selection fallback. The Console annotates 'kv_miss' and you can click through to the raw request log. Sometimes ASR labels it as 'K V cash' in the transcript export but it's KV cache.
[01:58] Owen: Can the Console link the trace to our application logs? We need correlation across our gateway.

[02:05] Diego: Yes — request IDs are plumbed through headers. Console has a 'stitch logs' feature, we match by X-Request-ID or the Trace-ID. See the right pane, I just pasted a gateway log and it lines up with the same request id so you can follow from ingress to model run.
[02:28] Lena: For compliance we need immutable audit logs and KMS-managed keys for model payloads. How does Redwood handle key management in Private deployments?

[02:38] Diego: In Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM — you retain keys, Redwood doesn't see plaintext keys. For Hosted we can do envelope encryption with Redwood KMS but we recommend Dedicated/Private if you require key custody. We'll add the KMS checklist in the security pack.
[02:58] Samir: From a product perspective, how do we do canary rollouts without disturbing latency SLOs?

[03:07] Maya: We support per-route rollout policies — percentage traffic splits, health-based automatic rollback, and model variants. The Console shows live SLOs and you can pin a route to a model version and ramp up. Diego, show the rollout dashboard?

[03:19] Diego: Yep — here's a canary we did. You can see error rates and per-token p50/p95 graphs. If errors spike, the routing policy can fallback to a cheaper/older model automatically. There's also an option to route by latency budget versus cost budget, which is useful when you have mixed SLAs.
[03:45] Priya: About that 'cheaper' fallback — does it change embeddings or output format? We can't have regression in schema during fallbacks.

[03:53] Diego: We do schema checks at the routing layer. If the variant produces incompatible outputs, the policy will not auto-fallback unless you opt in. For strict schema we recommend using the 'strict route' mode which disables auto fallback and keeps canary manual.
[04:10] Owen: Network question — we are in a strict VPC posture, can Redwood run in our VPC?

[04:16] Diego: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC-deployed control plane with customer-managed networking. For on-prem air-gapped setups we have an on-prem package as well. There are a couple of knobs around NAT and peering we'll share in the deployment guide.
[04:34] Priya: Diego, can you demo a real trace from our sample trace set we uploaded last week?

[04:40] Diego: I pulled one sample you labeled 'auth-flow-0926' — loading now. Ok, see the timeline: there's a 600ms stall at the routing layer then a per-token jitter spike at tokens 8-12. The Console flags the stall as 'route_requeue' which indicates a transient capacity routing and a fallback to a model variant.
[05:05] Priya: So route_requeue meaning it retried to another pod? That can increase tail latency.

[05:12] Diego: Exactly. We have two mitigations: reserved capacity (Dedicated) to reduce requeues, or smarter routing policies that prioritize low-latency instances. Also, prefix caching reduces repeated compute for common prompts.
[05:28] Samir: What's the unit economics of Dedicated? How big a commit do we need to avoid requeues at our 200 qps peak?

[05:36] Maya: We'll include a cost model in the SOW but short answer: Dedicated gives predictable throughput. We can run a capacity plan based on your peak QPS and typical token counts — Diego will run that micro-benchmark.
[05:51] Owen: Diego, on the Console traces, I noticed entries labeled 'kernel_fallback' — is that the runtime switching to a compatibility kernel?

[05:58] Diego: Yes. The runtime selects optimized kernels based on sequence length; if the optimized path isn't available (say quantized variant mismatch) it falls back to a generic kernel and you see higher per-token latencies. Console surfaces these events as 'kernel_fallback' with a pointer to the model variant.
[06:15] Priya: Is quantization something we need to worry about for correctness? We have strict numeric bit requirements for risk scoring.

[06:22] Diego: Quantization is a tradeoff — most open models preserve semantics at 4/8-bit but for numeric-sensitive workloads you might want 16-bit. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profile per workload and you can pin that profile per-model route.
[06:39] Lena: For audit, do you store request payloads? We can't keep PII in logs.

[06:45] Diego: By default we store request metadata and traces but not payloads unless you opt-in. For PII we support token redaction and masked logs. In Private, you can disable retention or route logs to your own S3 with server-side encryption.
[07:02] Priya: Diego, can you show the log stitch view where we jump from the trace to raw event lines?

[07:09] Diego: Sure — clicking the trace span shows the log slice: ingress headers, routing decisions, model runner stdout, and kernel events. Note the mis-typed field in our console export sometimes called 'req-id' vs 'request-id' — it's just an ASR/text artifact in the transcript export, the Console data is structured.
[07:34] Maya: Quick callout — we'll provide a guidance doc on header naming to make stitching deterministic.
[07:40] Samir: On observability, is there token-level cost attribution? Our finance team wants to see per-feature cost.

[07:47] Diego: Yes, Console has token accounting per-request and you can tag routes/features. The cost breakdown shows per-token compute, caching savings, and estimated downstream embedding cost. That helps inform batch vs streaming choices.
[08:04] Priya: Speaking of caching — we've seen KV cache low hit rates in production. Can Console help tune caching config?

[08:11] Diego: That's one of Optimize's features — it analyzes sequence distribution and suggests cache TTL, shard sizing, and prefix chunking. In Console we can simulate cache hit rates against historical data.
[08:26] Owen: Do you support sticky sessions to keep KV cache warm for frequent users?

[08:31] Diego: You can pin sessions to a runner for a short TTL. Sticky is a knob but it increases load balancing complexity. We typically use prefix caching plus request routing based on user id hash to improve locality.
[08:48] Priya: Can the Console detect prompt injection or unusual output patterns?

[08:52] Diego (slight stutter in transcript): We have heuristics — output validation, similarity-based anomaly detection, and schema checks. The Console surfaces anomalies and you can wire alerts to PagerDuty. Note: transcribed export may say 'pro-mpt' injection due to OCR, ignore that.
[09:12] Samir: Security again — SSO. We use SAML and require SCIM provisioning. Does Redwood Console support that?
[09:18] Maya: Yes. SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC, and audit logs. We'll include the specific IdP metadata fields in the security pack. Diego, also add the audit retention options.

[09:32] Diego: Will do. Also, we have a 'request replay' feature — you can replay an anonymized trace against a canary model to see behaviour differences. It's useful for regression testing during rollouts.
[09:50] Priya: Nice — can we replay with our own policy that censors PII?
[09:55] Diego: Yes, replay supports masking hooks and you can supply a scrubber lambda prior to replay. We'll send the example scrubber for your team to adapt.
[10:10] Owen: Back to latency — you mentioned automatic batching. Does that hurt tail latency? We need consistent p95 sub-300ms.

[10:18] Diego: Batching improves throughput but can add a batching delay. The runtime does continuous batching with latency-aware thresholds so short latency budgets bypass batching. Console shows the batching histogram so you can tune the threshold per-route.
[10:36] Priya: Any recommendations for our chat assistant, typical messages ~40 tokens, peak 200 qps?

[10:42] Diego: For that profile we recommend small batching window + prefix caching. If tail is critical, Dedicated reserved nodes sized to peak QPS reduces routing requeues. We'll run a benchmark on your 40-token sample to quantify.
[11:00] Maya: Let's walk through a failure path — Diego, trigger a simulated KV miss chain and show the trace playthrough.

[11:07] Diego: Ok injecting a simulated KV miss — you'll see the request fork to recompute, the route requeue, and then the fallback to a quantized variant. See the Console timeline: notice the 1.2s pause and then the model output. The trace also shows an increase in 'retries' metric.

[11:30] Priya: That's exactly the pattern we've been debugging. The Console's ability to annotate the reason is helpful. Can we get alerts on increases in 'route_requeue' and 'kernel_fallback' events?
[11:40] Diego: Yes, alert rules can be created in Console — threshold-based or anomaly-detection. We can also pipe alerts to your PagerDuty and Slack channels.
[11:52] Samir: On the POC, what's a realistic runbook?

[11:56] Maya: 3-week POC: week 1 - onboarding and sample trace ingestion + security review; week 2 - benchmarking and optimization (cache/quantization); week 3 - canary rollout and ops handoff. Deliverables: capacity plan, SLO dashboard, and SOW with cost.
[12:16] Priya: Ok that sounds good. Any extra security paperwork for our procurement?
[12:21] Lena: We'll need SOC2 Type II report, encryption details, and a data processing addendum (DPA).
[12:27] Maya: We'll include SOC2 evidence and DPA template, and Maya will follow up with contract contact. We'll also add an SSO/SCIM integration checklist.

[12:38] Diego: Quick demo of the 'trace diff' feature — I compare two traces side-by-side and Console highlights divergence points: output embeddings, latency, and token-level probability drift. This helps detect regressions after model updates.
[12:56] Priya: Can we export these diffs into a CSV for offline analysis?
[13:02] Diego: Yes, exportable. Also there's an API to query the Console traces programmatically if you want to integrate into your CI.
[13:18] Owen: On networking again — egress costs. If we choose Dedicated in a cloud region, do we pay Redwood egress or is it through our account?
[13:27] Maya: For Dedicated deployed in your VPC, egress is in your account. For Hosted you pay Redwood's egress costs as part of usage. We'll clarify pricing in the SOW.
[13:42] Samir: Any reference customers in finance who have similar compliance needs?
[13:47] Maya: We have a few anonymized case studies — banking and healthcare customers. I'll attach short references in the follow-up email.

[13:55] Diego: Back to trace mechanics — the Console stores spans with millisecond resolution. If you need even more granularity we can enable higher sampling, though that increases storage. In Private you can route spans to your storage backplane.
[14:12] Priya: Storage retention policies? Our legal requires 90 days of immutable audit logs.
[14:18] Diego: We support retention windows and immutable append-only stores for audits. We'll include retention config options in the pack.
[14:30] Samir: Are there known gotchas with our risk scoring models when migrating to quantized runners?

[14:36] Diego: Numeric drift is the main one. We recommend running a golden set regression via the replay feature and a set of unit prompts that validate thresholds. Optimize will also flag prompts with the largest drift.
[14:55] Priya: Can we set synthetic probes to run continuously to measure p95?
[15:02] Diego: Yes, synthetic monitors with canary probes into the route. They show up in SLO dashboards and can trigger alerts if p95 breaches.
[15:15] Maya: Quick housekeeping — we'll send the security pack, SOW, and a sample scrubber function. Any other blocker?
[15:23] Lena: Is there any encryption-in-transit specifics when using Private across peered accounts?
[15:29] Diego: TLS mutual auth is supported and we can layer mTLS between control plane and runners. We'll detail the network topology options.
[15:42] Priya: For the micro-benchmark, what metrics do you need from us?
[15:46] Diego: Sample inputs (anonymized), sequence length histogram, peak QPS, acceptable p95 target, and target model family. That lets us size Dedicated pools if needed.
[16:02] Priya: I'll gather those and share by Monday. Note: some of our samples contain test customer IDs — we'll scrub before upload.

[16:10] Maya: Perfect. Last demo piece: request playback — watch the console as I replay the trace. You can see output differences between model v1 and v1.1 and the diff highlights a token-level probability drop at token 12.
[16:28] Samir: That diff is exactly the kind of signal we need for A/B.
[16:33] Diego: One more note — sometimes in exported transcripts the product names get munged (e.g., 'Redwood Optimize' -> 'Redwood Opt-in'); ignore those ASR artifacts.
[16:48] Priya: Quick question — who will be our single technical contact at Redwood for the POC?
[16:53] Maya: Diego will be SE lead, Maya as AE. We'll also assign an onboarding engineer if the POC proceeds.
[17:02] Owen: What's the timeline for the security review? We usually need a week to run through the SOC/DPA docs.
[17:08] Lena: We'll aim to review within 7 business days after docs arrive.
[17:14] Maya: Great. Any more technical questions?
[17:18] Priya: One last: can the Console show per-tenant cost breakdown for multi-tenant workload?
[17:24] Diego: Yes, per-tenant tagging and cost attribution are supported; we can demo that in the POC.
[17:33] Samir: Ok that covers it for me.

[17:36] Maya: Recap — Redwood to send SOW + security pack + SSO checklist, Everbrook to share sample traces and load profile. POC kickoff week of 2026-10-20. Diego will run micro-bench and annotate console traces. Any objections?
[17:53] Priya: No objections. Looking forward to the POC.
[17:57] Lena: No objections from security side, pending docs.

[18:01] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with links: Deck (tinyurl.com/redwood-everbrook-deck), Bench sheet (drive.google.com/drive/redwood-everbrook-bench), and the security pack PDF. End recording.
[18:18] (call ends)
